tokensAndTheme.detail: The LDS runtime, theme boundary, and token ownership were reviewed for this surface.

decisions.outcome: Core styles load before the theme styles in the application entry.
The application root owns the font and automatic theme provider scope.
The surface inherits light, dark, and automatic theme behavior from the root.
Text and spacing values resolve through LDS semantic tokens.
No unapproved raw visual literal remains in the changed source.

layoutAndVisualFoundations.detail: Responsive layout and all applicable visual foundations were reviewed with representative content.

decisions.outcome: The section heading precedes status and refresh controls in reading order.
A single-column grid preserves the device-list information hierarchy.
The product container owns narrow wrapping and overflow behavior.
The heading and device count retain a clear semantic hierarchy.
Spacing uses LDS tokens and the other visual scales are not introduced here.

statePatternsAndMotion.detail: Ready and loading states, retained content, and motion disposition were reviewed for the region.

decisions.outcome: Ready and loading are rendered here; other states remain owned by the parent workflow.
An LDS Skeleton communicates loading within the device-list region.
Refresh keeps orchestration in product code and replaces only the list region.
This change introduces no product-owned motion or transition.

assetsIconographyAndBrand.detail: The device-list change introduces no icon, image, font, or brand asset.

contentAndInternationalization.detail: Visible copy, product voice, locale ownership, formatting, and truncation were reviewed.

decisions.outcome: The copy catalog records the heading, loading label, and refresh action.
Action-oriented labels follow the product writing and voice guidance.
The application shell remains the owner of document language and locale.
Only an integer count is displayed and no new locale-sensitive unit is added.
The narrow viewport evidence covers expansion and wrapping of translated labels.

accessibility.detail: Semantic order, keyboard behavior, accessible state, targets, contrast, and motion were reviewed.

decisions.outcome: The section heading and controls preserve a logical semantic DOM order.
The LDS Button remains keyboard reachable and refresh does not move focus.
The skeleton exposes a loading name and the button retains its accessible role.
The LDS Button supplies its owned target size and keyboard activation.
LDS tokens preserve contrast and loading is communicated without color alone.
No new motion is introduced, so reduced-motion behavior does not regress.

componentMapping.detail: Owner-package reuse and the remaining product orchestration boundary were explicitly reviewed.

decisions.outcome: Button and Skeleton come from the LDS core public export.
Existing LDS Button and Skeleton components are reused without a local clone.
The product surface continues to own device data and refresh orchestration.
No shared LDS authoring request or component exception remains.

verification.viewportDisposition: Normal and narrow layouts preserve hierarchy without clipped content.
verification.themeDisposition: Both supported color schemes preserve token ownership and contrast.
verification.stateDisposition: Ready and loading states remain distinguishable and keep the refresh path clear.
